picked.title: TouchBridge: Tactile-Conditioned Human-to-Robot Transfer for Dexterous Manipulation
picked.summary: Human demonstrations offer an efficient and scalable source of data for dexterous robot manipulation, but differences in sensing and hand morphology complicate the transfer of contact-rich interactions. We present TouchBridge, a hardware--software co-designed framework for human-to-robot data transformation. A wearable human demonstration interface and a corresponding robot interface establish cross-embodiment correspondence in visual and fingertip tactile sensing. We introduce Tac-Retarget, a tactile-conditioned retargeting method that uses measured contact to align fingertip contact patches and preserve their spatial relations within and across hands. Unlike object-aware or simulation-based transfer pipelines, Tac-Retarget requires no object mesh, object-pose estimate, or physics simulation for retargeting, enabling direct and scalable conversion of human demonstrations into robot-domain training data. Combined with visual synthesis and camera-anchored action conversion, TouchBridge produces robot-domain demonstrations for fine-tuning a pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) model. Across four real-world contact-rich tasks, policies fine-tuned solely on TouchBridge-converted human demonstrations achieve a 72.5% average success rate, compared with 77.5% using an equal number of teleoperated robot demonstrations, while human demonstration collection is 7.0x faster. Under the same policy and training setup, Tac-Retarget outperforms DexPilot and UniDex by 25.0 and 42.5 percentage points, respectively.

picked.title: Learning Event-based Obstacle Avoidance via Differentiable Simulation
picked.summary: Reliable obstacle avoidance is essential for safe quadrotor flight in unknown environments, yet conventional frame-based cameras remain challenged by motion blur, limited dynamic range, and latency under fast motion. Event cameras, with sub-millisecond latency, high dynamic range, and negligible motion blur, offer a promising alternative, but leveraging them for closed-loop control remains difficult. Existing approaches either adopt cascaded architectures that first estimate depth and then map it to control commands, introducing error propagation, or achieve end-to-end control through costly offline pretraining before online fine-tuning can even begin. We address these challenges with a CUDA-based event simulator that exploits GPU parallelism to render events efficiently within the training loop, integrated into a differentiable simulation pipeline that enables direct gradient backpropagation through the differentiable physics model, improving sample efficiency. This allows us to train an end-to-end policy that maps event frames directly to control commands, without intermediate depth estimation. We validate our approach through zero-shot real-world deployment on a quadrotor, achieving robust obstacle avoidance in both odometry-assisted and odometry-free settings, including under low-light conditions where conventional cameras typically fail.

picked.title: Utility-WAM: Correcting Future-Induced Action Changes
picked.summary: World Action Models (WAMs) can condition robot actions on generated visual futures, but this additional context is neither cost-free nor uniformly beneficial. We examine what a predicted future actually changes: the action delta $Δa$ between the future-conditioned and future-free execution paths of the same model. Under a shared WAM checkpoint, this delta barely shifts average benchmark success ($+0.8$ points on LIBERO, $-0.8$ on RoboTwin~2.0), while generating visual futures increases inference latency by 1.7--1.9$\times$. These aggregate metrics conceal a concentrated failure mode that we term \emph{future-induced negative transfer}: while predictive deltas benefit long-horizon tasks ($+2.4$ points on LIBERO-Long) and remain negligible on most routine manipulations, they induce severe degradation on precision tasks---with \emph{Press Stapler} and \emph{Place Can Basket} losing 54.0 and 34.0 points, recurring as top failure modes across independently trained WAM variants. We introduce \textbf{Utility-WAM} for in-place correction of future-conditioned control. Its primary learning component is a residual adapter that repairs future-induced velocity deltas under a frozen shared WAM by aligning them with ground-truth dynamic guidance and penalizing excess error beyond the future-free baseline. The adapter selectively eliminates the majority of severe task drops (reducing losses to 6.0 and 14.0 points) while preserving long-horizon foresight. To eliminate superfluous video computation, a lightweight pre-generation gate reuses counterfactual action outcomes to selectively bypass video generation on 75.5\% of RoboTwin queries, cutting latency by 38\% while improving average success to 93.3\% on RoboTwin~2.0 and 98.9\% on LIBERO. On physical bimanual manipulation across three real-world tasks, Utility-WAM succeeds in 53 of 60 trials, compared to 43 for FAST-WAM.

picked.title: How Much Should a VLA Trust Its Reasoning? Step-Level Guidance as a Measured Action-Value Function
picked.summary: Reasoning vision-language-action (VLA) policies write a reasoning trace and then decode the action from it. A wrong trace yields a wrong action, and even a correct-looking trace can mislead the plan. Existing remedies ask whether the reasoning is right. We ask how strongly it should steer. CoC-CFG applies classifier-free guidance between the policy's context and the same context without the reasoning span. One weight per Euler step attenuates or amplifies the reasoning, and w=1 recovers the original policy. We treat the choice of this weight as a Markov decision process whose action values are measured, not bootstrapped. With the expert frozen and the noise fixed, applying a weight for one step and finishing the plan under the current controller returns that weight's value exactly. Q-adaptive guidance fits these values with small critics and improves the controller conservatively. In the Alpasim driving simulator it outperforms every fixed weight and online RL (SAC, GRPO) in open loop, and in closed loop it passes 262 of 300 scenes, against 252 for the original policy. On held-out frames of the Waymo end-to-end driving benchmark, its first three stages outperform every fixed weight, four adaptive-guidance methods, SAC and GRPO. On the hidden test set, a frozen Alpamayo 1.5 with rule-based camera and vehicle conversions and Q-adaptive guidance sets a new state of the art among published methods: 8.135159 rater feedback score, against 8.079 for the best published method.

智能驾驶进入物理AI时代？7位行业嘉宾给出最新判断
picked.summary: 10月26日，第八届智能驾驶大会暨2026环秀湖物理AI产业发展推介会在苏州相城举行。 上一届，车路云一体化、智能驾驶出海和无人驾驶商业化是讨论重点，而到了今年，大会的讨论边界进一步从智能驾驶向物理AI延伸。 世界模型、强化学习、端侧智能、虚拟仿真、Robotaxi之外，机器人、低空飞行器等不同形态的物理智能开始出现在同一场大会上。这背后，是智能驾驶行业正在面对的一组新问题。 一方面，高阶辅助驾驶已经进入规模化上车阶段，Robotaxi也开始从技术验证走向运营和商业化；另一方面，当AI真正进入汽车、机器人、飞行器等物理设备，如何获得足够的数据、如何训练和验证模型、如何降低开发成本，以及如何保证系统在真实世界中的安全性，正在成为新的技术难题。 当天，包括Momenta、曹操出行、面壁智能等企业，以及高校和科研机构的多位嘉宾，从世界模型、强化学习、端侧大模型、虚拟仿真、车路云和物理AI基础设施等方向给出了自己的判断。 总结这些发言不难发现，智能驾驶正在成为物理AI最早进入现实世界的一块试验场。而从一辆车的自动驾驶，到机器人、低空飞行器以及城市交通系统，不同技术路线正在回答同一个问题：AI如何从数字世界真正进入物理世界，并形成可以规模化运行的产品。 中国工程院院士，清华大学车辆与运载学院教授、智能绿色车辆与交通全国重点实验室主任 李克强 关键词：智能驾驶安全、车路云一体化、单车智能瓶颈 …

picked.title: 伯牙智能刘欣：GPT-6 之后，轮到硬件拖机器人后腿了 | 物理AI 50人
picked.summary: 灵巧手去年出货近 2 万只，大部分在「吃灰」 作者丨 向 欣 编辑丨 高景辉 去年，国内灵巧手公开可查的出货量是约两万只。在伯牙智能创始人刘欣的观察里，其中大部分灵巧手的归宿是跟着人形机器人表演几场，然后被搁在角落里， 「表演完就吃灰」 。 便宜的低自由度灵巧手多用于表演；操作能力更强的高自由度产品又容易损坏，有的因为贵，买回来供着不敢用，有的用一星期到两三个月就坏了——这是刘欣看到的灵巧手市场的现状。 在他看来，灵巧手行业连目标客户是谁、要解决什么问题、客户愿意为什么买单，都还没有明确答案。行业需要开辟 第三个市场 ：以可接受的成本，将科研级操作能力带入实际应用。 而这样的产品至今仍未出现，目前最顶尖的灵巧手，离人手能力都相差甚远。这就是伯牙的机会。 刘欣在阿里工作近十年，曾任阿里巴巴操作系统事业部技术总监、斑马智行产品负责人，业务涉及手机、汽车、IoT 和机器人。2023 年，他加入蔚来，负责乐道汽车智能化相关产品。 2024 年 8 月，他联合斑马智行联合创始人张斯成，以及哈尔滨工业大学（深圳）、中国科学技术大学的两位教授创办伯牙智能，希望「为人工智能造一双真正能干活的手」。 跨行业的经历，让他习惯把一件事放进更大的坐标系里思考，做灵巧手也是如此。他喜欢从不同领域里寻找灵巧手的产品思路，思考市场的迭代和发展方向，会参照汽车和手机的发展历程，也会从生物进化和人体结构出发，思考五指设计的必要性；旁征博引，各种论据信手拈来。 由此，他形成了一些与行业主流判断不同的看法： 相比硬件，模型可能更早触及能力拐点 …

picked.title: 让触觉像视觉一样可规模化，哥大李昀烛团队 FlexiTac 的开源实践 | IROS 2026
picked.summary: FlexiTac压阻式传感器可兼顾柔性、低成本与一致性。机器人的视觉能力正快速增强，但 触觉仍然是具身智能系统中的薄弱环节 。尤其是在精细操作场景中，当 物体被遮挡、透明、易碎，或需要精确判断接触力与手内姿态 时，仅靠视觉往往难以确认机器人是否真正抓稳了物体、是否发生了滑移，也难以实现可靠的力控与顺从交互。 与图像领域已经形成相对统一的传感器和数据体系相比，触觉研究尚未形成类似的「收敛」。不同实验室往往使用不同类型的触觉传感器，但它们都面临 寿命、柔性、多维信息感知、分辨率、成本与一致性 难以同时兼顾的困境。这使得触觉数据采集、算法研究以及不同系统之间的复现都变得更加困难。 如何 让触觉像视觉一样 ，成为一种可以被更多机器人使用、被大量采集、被算法反复利用的基础感知能力？ 针对这个问题，哥伦比亚大学李昀烛团队提出了开源柔性压阻式触觉传感器平台 FlexiTac 。在本届 IROS 2026 的触觉专题研讨会上，李昀烛系统介绍了这一平台开源一年半后的进展与生态。 FlexiTac 是一套低成本、开源、可扩展的 压阻式柔性触觉传感器 ，团队同时开源了完整 BOM、详细组装说明以及用于读取触觉数据的软件。 FlexiTac 采用 FPC 与力敏薄膜层叠结构，组装仅需 3 分钟，可弯曲、裁剪并包裹于不同几何表面，适配手套、指尖或机器人皮肤等多种形态。 其核心优势在于 成本低、制作简单、高度柔性与可扩展、以及较好的长期稳定性和批次一致性 …
